name: Cooker control unit
summary: Plan mark for the double-pole control switch and outlet serving a fixed cooking appliance.
description: A cooker control unit is a high-current double-pole switch, sometimes with an auxiliary socket outlet, that controls and isolates a fixed cooker or hob. Plan legends usually draw a switch box with the letters CCU or a cooker mark, placed within reach of the appliance but not above the hob.

The symbol tells the electrician to run a dedicated radial circuit sized for the appliance, often 32 A or larger, and to install a separate cooker connection plate behind the appliance. Two symbols are often shown together: the control unit on the splashback and the connection outlet low behind the cooker. It does not show the cable size or the diversity used in the design. Those belong in the circuit schedule.
readingNotes: Look for a paired connection plate behind the appliance position.
Check whether the unit includes an auxiliary outlet.
drawingChecklist: State switch rating and auxiliary outlet requirement.
distinction: A general isolator mark has no auxiliary outlet and is not tied to a cooking appliance; the cooker control unit is a dedicated appliance accessory.
